turns.t: Doctor, I'm Meera, her daughter-in-law. Mrs Rao has had a dry mouth and sores under her dentures for a good while now.
Thank you for coming with her. Mrs Rao, tell me about your mouth.
It's so dry, I can't taste anything. And the sores hurt when I eat.
Where are the sores?
On the roof of my mouth, and on the gums at the front.
She's been eating only soft things for a few weeks.
Do the dentures still fit well? ~
They've been loose since the winter. ~
She had them made years ago. Her face has changed since then. ~
Do you take them out at night? ~
No, I forget. I sleep in them. ~
That can make the sores worse. How long have you had the sores?
Three weeks.
Any fever, or sore throat? ~
No, nothing like that. ~
Doctor, shall I look in her mouth and record what I see for the notes? ~
Yes, please do. I'd like to see it myself too. ~
Will it hurt? ~
No, I'll be very gentle. Open wide, Mrs Rao.
There are red, inflamed patches under the upper denture, with some white coating, and the mouth is dry.
What is it, doctor? ~
It looks like denture stomatitis, with thrush on top, and the dry mouth makes it more likely. ~
What causes the dry mouth? ~
Often tablets, or not drinking enough, or other things. I'd like to look at her medicines list and arrange some blood tests.
I've brought her list. ~
Thank you. In the meantime, she should take the dentures out at night, and keep them in a cup of water.
I'll try to remember. ~
I'll remind her every evening. ~
Brush the gums with a soft brush, and sip water through the day. ~
I will. ~
I'll also refer you to the dentist to have the dentures checked or remade.
Thank you, doctor. ~
